prompt: Complete LineAppender: appendLine must append a line (plus newline) to a file, creating the file if it does not exist, and lineCount must return how many lines the file contains.
explanation: Files.writeString normally truncates an existing file, but StandardOpenOption flags change that: CREATE makes the file if it is missing, and APPEND adds to the end instead of overwriting. Files.readAllLines reads the whole file into a List<String>, so counting lines is just calling size() on the result. These one-line NIO calls replace the manual reader/writer loops needed with older APIs.
hints: Files.writeString accepts StandardOpenOption varargs after the content.
Combine StandardOpenOption.CREATE and StandardOpenOption.APPEND, and remember to add "\n" to the line yourself.
Files.readAllLines(p) gives you a List<String>; its size() is the line count.
